A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CDTD research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–U. Full-document text and visual comparisons support reliable judgments without material evidence gaps.

before.justification: v4 reports original CDTD benchmark experiments, component ablations, sensitivity analyses, and timing measurements in Section 4 and the appendices, including Tables 1–2 and Appendices S–U.

after.justification: v5 retains the original CDTD experimental results, including benchmark performance, ablations, sensitivity analyses, and training and sampling measurements.

M1.justification: The architecture, losses, adaptive noise schedules, and sampling procedure in Sections 2–3 and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Appendix B corrects the mathematical identification of the existing denoiser and score without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same eleven datasets listed in Table 3 for tabular synthesis and downstream regression or binary classification. The task conversions and supplementary evaluation scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain SMOTE, ARF, CTGAN, TVAE, TabDDPM, CoDi, and TabSyn. Corresponding comparisons retain the same participation and dataset-specific exclusions, including those documented in Appendix S.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendices H–L retain the same preprocessing, 60/20/20 data splits, evaluation metrics, model configurations, training budgets, and sampling settings. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Table 2 and Appendix T, sampling-step sensitivity in Table 6, initialization sensitivity in Tables 7–8, and qualitative and correlation analyses in Appendices P–R are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report five synthetic-data sampling seeds and ten downstream-model seeds. The standard-error and standard-deviation reporting practices in the detailed benchmark and ablation tables are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical results, rankings, plotted findings, and result entries match throughout both PDFs. For example, Table 11 retains CDTD per-type detection score 0.739 and correlation-matrix distance 0.684; the detailed results in Appendices S–U also match.

T1.justification: Appendix B corrects the identification of c_skip x_t + c_out F_theta from the score s_theta to the denoiser xhat_theta, and explicitly states s_theta = (xhat_theta - x_t)/sigma(t)^2. This corrects a local mathematical inconsistency in the loss-calibration derivation; the proposition and remaining proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about unified continuous diffusion, feature homogenization, adaptive noise schedules, scalability, and empirical performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of noise-schedule performance and data-space diffusion remain unchanged. The limitations concerning hyperparameters, privacy, specialized data types, and imputation are also retained without substantive revision.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures and code/data access information are unchanged, including the hyperparameters, RTX 4090 hardware, 30,000 training steps, and default 200-step sampler documented in the appendices.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning in the introduction and Appendices N–O are unchanged. The new publication header does not revise the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v5 adds the ICLR 2025 publication header, updates the arXiv version stamp, and makes a short explanatory revision in Appendix B distinguishing the denoiser from the score. The narrative and section structure otherwise match.

P2.justification: v5 adds a running publication header and locally reflows Appendices B–C across pages 15–17. There are small spacing differences in Tables 9–10, while figure content, captions, and table organization remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v5 corrects the misleading denoiser/score identification in Appendix B and explicitly gives their noise-scaled relationship, improving mathematical accuracy and consistency with the existing sampling derivation in Appendix L. This is a limited quality gain: the methods, empirical evidence, and conclusions remain unchanged, and the other edits are minor presentation changes.
